plan: 1 Kings 13:1-34; 1 Kings 14:1-18, 21-24; 2 Chronicles 12:13-14; 2 Chronicles 11:18-23; 2 Chronicles 12:1-12; 1 Kings 14:25-28; 2 Chronicles 12:15-16; 1 Kings 14:29-31; 1 Kings 15:1-5; 2 Chronicles 13:1–14:1; 1 Kings 15:6-8; 2 Chronicles 14:2-8; 1 Kings 15:9-15; 1 Kings 14:19-20; 1 Kings 15:25-26, 27-34; 2 Chronicles 14:9-15; 2 Chronicles 15:1-19

readings.title: The Word Against the Counterfeit Altar
readings.subtitle: A man of Elohim from Yehuḏah executes divine judgment on Yaroḇ‛am's unsanctioned system.
readings.text: [1 Kings 13:1] And see, a man of <dn>Elohim</dn> went from Yehuḏah to Běyth Ěl by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, while Yaroḇ‛am was standing by the slaughter-place to burn incense. [2] And he cried out against the slaughter-place by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, <dq>“O slaughter-place, slaughter-place! Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘See, a son is to be born to the house of Daviḏ, Yoshiyahu is his name. And on you he shall slaughter <dn>את</dn> the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and men’s bones be burned on you.’ ”</dq> [3] And he gave a sign the same day, saying, <dq>“This is the sign which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken: See, the slaughter-place is split apart, and the ashes on it is poured out.”</dq> [4] And it came to be when Sovereign Yaroḇ‛am heard the saying of the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, who cried out against the slaughter-place in Běyth Ěl, that he stretched out <dn>את</dn> his hand from the slaughter-place, saying, “Seize him!” Then his hand, which he stretched out toward him, dried up, so that he was unable to bring it back to him. [5] And the slaughter-place was split apart, and the ashes poured out from the slaughter-place, according to the sign which the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> had given by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] And the sovereign answered and said to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Please appease <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and pray for me, that my hand might be restored to me.” And the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> appeased the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the sovereign’s hand was restored to him, and became as it was before. [7] The sovereign then said to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I give you a gift.” [8] But the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> said to the sovereign, “If you were to give me half your house, I do not go in with you, nor do I eat bread nor drink water in this place. [9] “For so <dn>He</dn> commanded me by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, <dq>‘Do not eat bread, nor drink water, nor return by the same way you came.’ ”</dq> [10] So he went another way and did not return by the way he came to Běyth Ěl.

readings.title: The Snare of the Old Prophet
readings.subtitle: Deception and the fatal cost of compromising the direct command of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [1 Kings 13:11] And a certain old prophet was dwelling in Běyth Ěl, and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> had done that day in Běyth Ěl, the words which he had spoken to the sovereign. [12] And their father said to them, “Which way did he go?” And his sons had seen which way the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> went who came from Yehuḏah. [13] And he said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” And they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode on it, [14] and went after the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and found him sitting under a terebinth. And he said to him, “Are you the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> who came from Yehuḏah?” And he said, “I am.” [15] And he said to him, “Come home with me and eat bread.” [16] And he said, “I am not able to return with you or to go in with you, nor am I to eat bread or drink water with you in this place. [17] “For word came to me by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Do not eat bread nor drink water there, nor return by going the way you came.’ ”</dq> [18] And he said to him, “I too am a prophet like you, and a messenger spoke to me by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, <dq>‘Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water.’ ”</dq> But he lied to him. [19] So he turned back with him, and ate bread in his house, and drank water. [20] And it came to be, as they sat at the table, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to the prophet who had brought him back, [21] and he cried out to the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> who came from Yehuḏah, saying, <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘Because you have rebelled against <dn>את</dn> the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and have not guarded <dn>את</dn> the command which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded you,</dq> [22] <dq>and turned back, and ate bread, and drank water in the place of which <dn>He</dn> said to you, “Do not eat bread nor drink water,” your body shall not enter the burial-site of your fathers.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Unyielding Verdict of the Lion
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH enforces His word on the disobedient prophet, yet the house of Yaroḇ‛am persists in high treason.
readings.text: [1 Kings 13:23] And it came to be, after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back. [24] And he went, and a lion met him on the way and killed him. And his body was thrown on the way. And the donkey was standing by it, and the lion was standing by the body. [25] And see, men were passing by and saw the body thrown on the way, while the lion was standing by the body. And they went and reported it in the city where the old prophet dwelt. [26] And the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard it, and said, “It is the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> who rebelled against the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave him to the lion, and it tore him apart and killed him, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke to him.” [27] And he spoke to his sons, saying, “Saddle the donkey for me.” And they saddled it. [28] So he went and found his body thrown on the way, and the donkey and the lion standing by the body. The lion had not eaten the body nor mauled the donkey. [29] And the prophet lifted up <dn>את</dn> the body of the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and placed it on the donkey, and brought it back. And the old prophet came to the city to mourn, and to bury him, [30] and he placed his body in his own burial-site. And they lamented over him, saying, “Oh, my brother!” [31] And it came to be, after he had buried him, that he spoke to his sons, saying, “When I am dead, then you shall bury me in the burial-site where the man of <dn>Elohim</dn> is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones. [32] “For the word which he cried out, by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, against the slaughter-place in Běyth Ěl, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Shomeron, shall certainly come to be.” [33] After this event Yaroḇ‛am did not turn from his evil way, but again he made priests from all sorts of people for the high places. Whoever wished, he ordained, to become one of the priests of the high places. [34] And this matter was the sin of the house of Yaroḇ‛am, even to cut it off and destroy it from the face of the earth.

readings.title: Seeking the Seer in Disguise
readings.subtitle: Yaroḇ‛am attempts to subvert prophetic sight through deception in the face of his son's illness.
readings.text: [1 Kings 14:1] At that time Aḇiyah the son of Yaroḇ‛am became sick. [2] And Yaroḇ‛am said to his wife, “Please arise, and disguise yourself, so they do not know that you are the wife of Yaroḇ‛am, and go to Shiloh. See, Aḥiyah the prophet is there, who spoke to me of becoming sovereign over this people. [3] “And you shall take with you ten loaves, and cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. Let him declare to you what becomes of the child.” [4] And Yaroḇ‛am’s wife did so, and rose up and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Aḥiyah. But Aḥiyahu was unable to see, for his eyes had set because of his age. [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to Aḥiyahu, <dq>“See, the wife of Yaroḇ‛am is coming to ask you a word about her son, for he is sick. Speak to her thus and thus. For it shall be, when she comes in, that she makes herself strange.”</dq> [6] And it came to be, when Aḥiyahu heard the sound of her footsteps as she came through the door, he said, “Come in, wife of Yaroḇ‛am. Why are you making yourself strange? And I have been sent to you with a hard word.

readings.title: The Decree of Total Eradication
readings.subtitle: Aḥiyahu pronounces the absolute destruction of Yaroḇ‛am’s rebellious lineage.
readings.text: [7] Go, say to Yaroḇ‛am, <dq>‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “Because <dn>I</dn> exalted you from among the people, and made you ruler over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl,</dq> [8] <dq>and tore the reign away from the house of Daviḏ, and gave it to you – and you have not been as <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, who guarded <dn>My</dn> commands and who followed <dn>Me</dn> with all his heart, to do only what was right in <dn>My</dn> eyes,</dq> [9] <dq>but you have done more evil than all who were before you, for you have gone and made for yourself other mighty ones and moulded images to provoke <dn>Me</dn>, and have cast <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn> behind your back –</dq> [10] <dq>therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil to the house of Yaroḇ‛am, and shall cut off from Yaroḇ‛am <dn>את</dn> every male in Yisra’ěl, whether shut up or left at large, and sweep away the remnant of the house of Yaroḇ‛am, as one sweeps away dung until it is all gone.</dq> [11] <dq>Those of Yaroḇ‛am who die in the city the dogs do eat, and those who die in the field the birds of the heavens do eat, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken it!” ’</dq> [12] <dq>“And you, arise, go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child shall die.</dq> [13] <dq>“And all Yisra’ěl shall mourn for him and bury him, for he is the only one of Yaroḇ‛am who shall come to the burial-site, because in him there is found a good report toward <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, in the house of Yaroḇ‛am.</dq> [14] <dq>“And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall raise up for <dn>Himself</dn> a sovereign over Yisra’ěl who cuts off the house of Yaroḇ‛am, this day, and even now!</dq> [15] <dq>“And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall strike Yisra’ěl, as a reed is shaken in the water, and shall pluck <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from this good soil which <dn>He</dn> gave to their fathers, and shall scatter them beyond the River, because they made their Ashěrim, provoking <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [16] <dq>and <dn>He</dn> shall give Yisra’ěl up, because of the sins of Yaroḇ‛am, who sinned and who made Yisra’ěl sin.”</dq>

readings.title: The Immediate Toll of Rebellion
readings.subtitle: The child expires as the prophecy against the apostate house officially commences.
readings.text: [17] And the wife of Yaroḇ‛am rose up and went, and came to Tirtsah. When she came to the threshold of the house, the child died. [18] And they buried him, and all Yisra’ěl lamented for him, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke through <dn>His</dn> servant Aḥiyahu the prophet.

readings.subsection: The Rot of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Terminal Rot of Yehuḏah
readings.subtitle: Reḥaḇ‛am abandons the Torah and plunges the Southern Kingdom into systemic abomination.
readings.text: [1 Kings 14:19] And the rest of the acts of Yaroḇ‛am, how he fought and how he reigned, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl. [20] And the days that Yaroḇ‛am reigned was twenty-two years. So he slept with his fathers, and Naḏaḇ his son reigned in his place. [21] Meanwhile Reḥaḇ‛am son of Shelomoh reigned in Yehuḏah. Reḥaḇ‛am was forty-one years old when he became sovereign, and he reigned seventeen years in Yerushalayim, the city which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, to put <dn>His</dn> Name there. And his mother’s name was Na‛amah the Ammonitess. [22] And Yehuḏah did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and they provoked <dn>Him</dn> to jealousy with their sins which they committed, more than all that their fathers had done. [23] For they also built for themselves high places, and pillars, and Ashěrim on every high hill and under every green tree. [24] And there were also cult prostitutes in the land. They did according to all the abominations of the nations which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> dispossessed before the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.subsection: The Rot of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Stripping of the Treasuries
readings.subtitle: Shishaq of Mitsrayim extracts the accumulated wealth of Shelomoh due to national apostasy.
readings.text: [1 Kings 14:25] And it came to be, in the fifth year of Sovereign Reḥaḇ‛am, that Shishaq sovereign of Mitsrayim came up against Yerushalayim. [26] And he took away <dn>את</dn> the treasures of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the treasures of the sovereign’s house, he even took away all. And he took away all <dn>את</dn> the shields of gold which Shelomoh had made. [27] And Sovereign Reḥaḇ‛am made shields of bronze to replace them, and entrusted them into the hands of the chiefs of the guard, who guarded the entrance of the sovereign’s house. [28] And it came to be, whenever the sovereign went into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the guards would bring them, then take them back into the guardroom. [29] And the rest of the acts of Reḥaḇ‛am, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [30] And there was fighting between Reḥaḇ‛am and Yaroḇ‛am all the days. [31] So Reḥaḇ‛am slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ. And the name of his mother was Na‛amah the Ammonitess. And Aḇiyam his son reigned in his place.

readings.subsection: The Rot of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Immediate Fruit of Forsaking Torah
readings.subtitle: Shishaq is deployed as an instrument of retributive discipline against Yehuḏah.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 12:1] And it came to be, when Reḥaḇ‛am had established the reign and had strengthened himself, that he forsook the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and all Yisra’ěl with him. [2] And it came to be, in the fifth year of Sovereign Reḥaḇ‛am, that Shishaq sovereign of Mitsrayim came up against Yerushalayim – because they had trespassed against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – [3] with twelve hundred chariots, and sixty thousand horsemen, and innumerable people who came with him out of Mitsrayim: the Luḇim, the Sukkites and the Kushites. [4] And he took the cities of defence of Yehuḏah and came to Yerushalayim. [5] And Shemayah the prophet came to Reḥaḇ‛am and the rulers of Yehuḏah, who had been gathered in Yerushalayim because of Shishaq, and said to them, <dq>“Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘You have forsaken <dn>Me</dn>, and therefore <dn>I</dn> also have left you in the hand of Shishaq.’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Rot of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: Submission to the Righteous Decree
readings.subtitle: The sovereign humbles himself, averting total annihilation yet entering servitude.
readings.text: [6] Then the rulers of Yisra’ěl and the sovereign humbled themselves, and they said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is righteous.” [7] And when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw that they humbled themselves, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Shemayah, saying, <dq>“They have humbled themselves. <dn>I</dn> do not destroy them, but <dn>I</dn> shall give to them some deliverance, and not pour out <dn>My</dn> wrath on Yerushalayim by the hand of Shishaq,</dq> [8] <dq>but they are to become his servants, so that they know <dn>My</dn> service and the service of the reigns of the lands.”</dq> [9] And Shishaq sovereign of Mitsrayim came up against Yerushalayim, and took away <dn>את</dn> the treasures of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the treasures of the sovereign’s house. <dn>He</dn> took all, he also took <dn>את</dn> the gold shields which Shelomoh had made. [10] And Sovereign Reḥaḇ‛am made bronze shields to replace them and committed them into the hands of the chiefs of the guard, who guarded the entrance of the sovereign’s house. [11] And it came to be, whenever the sovereign went into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the guard would go and bring them out, then they would take them back into the guardroom. [12] And when he humbled himself, the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned from him, so as not to destroy him completely. And matters also went well in Yehuḏah.

readings.subsection: The Rot of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Legacy of an Unprepared Heart
readings.subtitle: Reḥaḇ‛am concludes his reign defined by a failure to seek YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 12:13] So Sovereign Reḥaḇ‛am strengthened himself in Yerushalayim and reigned. For Reḥaḇ‛am was forty-one years old when he became sovereign, and he reigned seventeen years in Yerushalayim, the city which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had chosen out of all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, to put <dn>His</dn> Name there. And his mother’s name was Na‛amah, the Ammonitess. [14] And he did evil, because he did not prepare his heart to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] And the acts of Reḥaḇ‛am, the first and the last, are they not written in the book of Shemayah the prophet, and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And there was fighting between Reḥaḇ‛am and Yaroḇ‛am all the days. [16] So Reḥaḇ‛am slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Daviḏ. And Aḇiyah his son reigned in his place.

readings.subsection: The Consolidation of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Divine Halt to Civil War
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH forbids Yehuḏah from striking their brothers in Yisra’ěl.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 11:1] And when Reḥaḇ‛am came to Yerushalayim, he assembled from the house of Yehuḏah and Binyamin one hundred and eighty thousand chosen brave men to fight against Yisra’ěl, to bring back the reign to Reḥaḇ‛am. [2] But the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Shemayahu the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, saying, [3] “Speak to Reḥaḇ‛am son of Shelomoh, sovereign of Yehuḏah, and to all Yisra’ěl in Yehuḏah and Binyamin, saying, [4] <dq>Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Do not go up or fight against your brothers! Let every man return to his house, for this matter is from <dn>Me</dn>.” ’ ”</dq> So they obeyed the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and turned back from going against Yaroḇ‛am.

readings.subsection: The Consolidation of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Physical Fortification of Yehuḏah
readings.subtitle: Reḥaḇ‛am establishes cities of defense and strengthens the borders.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 11:5] And Reḥaḇ‛am dwelt in Yerushalayim, and built cities for a defence in Yehuḏah. [6] And he built Běyth Leḥem, and Ěytam, and Teqova, [7] and Běyth Tsur, and Soḵo, and Aḏullam, [8] and Gath, and Marěshah, and Ziph, [9] and Aḏorayim, and Laḵish, and Azěqah, [10] and Tsor‛ah, and Ayalon, and Ḥeḇron, which are in Yehuḏah and Binyamin, cities of defence. [11] And he strengthened the strongholds, and put commanders in them, and stores of food, and oil, and wine, [12] and shields and spears in every city, and made them very strong. Thus Yehuḏah and Binyamin were his.

readings.subsection: The Consolidation of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Gathering of the Qadosh Remnant
readings.subtitle: The priests and the faithful abandon Yaroḇ‛am’s counterfeit system for Yerushalayim.
readings.text: [13] And from all their borders the priests and the Lěvites who were in all Yisra’ěl took their stand with him. [14] For the Lěvites left their open lands and their possessions and came to Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, for Yaroḇ‛am and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests unto <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [15] as he appointed for himself priests for the high places, and for goats, and the calf idols which he had made. [16] And after the Lěvites left, those from all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, such as set their heart to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, came to Yerushalayim to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers. [17] And they strengthened the reign of Yehuḏah, and made Reḥaḇ‛am son of Shelomoh strong for three years, for they walked in the way of Daviḏ and Shelomoh for three years.

readings.subsection: The Consolidation of the Southern Kingdom
readings.title: The Multiplication of Reḥaḇ‛am's Lineage
readings.subtitle: The sovereign secures his dynasty and disperses his heirs across the defended cities.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 11:18] And Reḥaḇ‛am took for himself as wife Maḥalath the daughter of Yerimoth son of Daviḏ, and of Aḇiḥayil the daughter of Eliyaḇ son of Yishai. [19] And she bore him sons: Ye‛ush, and Shemaryah, and Zaham. [20] And after her he took Ma‛aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇshalom. And she bore him Aḇiyah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith. [21] And Reḥaḇ‛am loved Ma‛aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇshalom more than all his wives and his concubines. For he had taken eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and brought forth twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters. [22] And Reḥaḇ‛am appointed Aḇiyah son of Ma‛aḵah as chief, to be leader among his brothers, in order to make him reign. [23] And he had understanding, and dispersed some of his sons throughout all the lands of Yehuḏah and Binyamin, to all the cities of defence, and gave them ample provision. And he sought many wives for them.

readings.title: The Fractured Heart of Aḇiyam
readings.subtitle: A reign of sin preserved only by the enduring covenant guarantee given to Daviḏ.
readings.text: [1 Kings 15:1] And in the eighteenth year of Sovereign Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, Aḇiyam became sovereign over Yehuḏah. [2] He reigned three years in Yerushalayim, and his mother’s name was Ma‛aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇishalom. [3] And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him, and his heart was not perfect to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>, as was the heart of his father Daviḏ. [4] But for Daviḏ’s sake <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> gave him a lamp in Yerushalayim, to raise up his son after him and by establishing Yerushalayim, [5] for Daviḏ did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and did not turn aside from all that <dn>He</dn> commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriyah the Ḥittite. [6] And there was fighting between Reḥaḇ‛am and Yaroḇ‛am all the days of his life. [7] And the rest of the acts of Aḇiyam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? And there was fighting between Aḇiyam and Yaroḇ‛am. [8] So Aḇiyam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Daviḏ. And Asa his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Resurgence of Righteousness
readings.subtitle: Asa purges the cult prostitutes and dismantles the abominable images of his fathers.
readings.text: [1 Kings 15:9] And in the twentieth year of Yaroḇ‛am sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Asa became sovereign over Yehuḏah. [10] And he reigned forty-one years in Yerushalayim, and his grandmother’s name was Ma‛aḵah the granddaughter of Aḇishalom. [11] And Asa did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as his father Daviḏ had done, [12] and put away the cult prostitutes from the land, and removed <dn>את</dn> all the idols that his fathers had made. [13] And he also removed <dn>את</dn> Ma‛aḵah his grandmother from being sovereigness mother, because she had made an abominable image for Ashěrah. And Asa cut down <dn>את</dn> her abominable image and burned it by the wadi Qiḏron. [14] But the high places were not removed. However, Asa’s heart was perfect with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all his days. [15] And he brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>את</dn> the set-apart items of his father, and his own set-apart items: silver and gold and utensils.

readings.title: A Compromised Alliance
readings.subtitle: Asa exhausts the treasuries to secure a treaty with Aram against Ba‛asha.
readings.text: [1 Kings 15:16] And there was fighting between Asa and Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl all their days. [17] And Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl came up against Yehuḏah, and built Ramah, to keep anyone from going out or coming in to Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah. [18] And Asa took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the treasuries of the sovereign’s house, and gave them into the hand of his servants. And Sovereign Asa sent them to Ben-Haḏaḏ son of Taḇrimmon, son of Ḥezyon, sovereign of Aram, who dwelt in Dammeseq, saying, [19] “Let there be a covenant between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you a present of silver and gold. Come, break your covenant with Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl, so that he withdraws from me.” [20] And Ben-Haḏaḏ listened to Sovereign Asa, and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Yisra’ěl, and struck Iyon, and Dan, and Aḇěl Běyth Ma‛aḵah, and all Kinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali. [21] And it came to be, when Ba‛asha heard it, that he stopped building Ramah, and remained in Tirtsah.

readings.title: The Dismantling of Ramah
readings.subtitle: Yehuḏah repurposes the enemy's timber before Asa's final days.
readings.text: [22] Then Sovereign Asa summoned all Yehuḏah – none was exempted – and they took away <dn>את</dn> the stones and <dn>את</dn> timber of Ramah, which Ba‛asha had used for building. And with them Sovereign Asa built Geḇa of Binyamin, and Mitspah. [23] And the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet. [24] So Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ his father. And Yehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Bloody Fulfillment of Prophecy
readings.subtitle: Ba‛asha seizes the throne and annihilates every breathing heir of Yaroḇ‛am.
readings.text: [1 Kings 15:25] And Naḏaḇ son of Yaroḇ‛am became sovereign over Yisra’ěl in the second year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, and he reigned over Yisra’ěl two years. [26] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin by which he had made Yisra’ěl sin. [27] Then Ba‛asha son of Aḥiyah, of the house of Yissasḵar, conspired against him. And Ba‛asha struck him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, for Naḏaḇ and all Yisra’ěl had laid siege to Gibbethon. [28] And Ba‛asha killed him in the third year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, and reigned in his place. [29] And it came to be, when he became sovereign, that he struck <dn>את</dn> all the house of Yaroḇ‛am. <dn>He</dn> did not leave to Yaroḇ‛am anyone breathing, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had spoken by <dn>His</dn> servant Aḥiyah the Shilonite, [30] because of the sins of Yaroḇ‛am, which he had sinned and by which he had made Yisra’ěl sin, because of his provocation with which he had provoked <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Perpetuation of the Counterfeit System
readings.subtitle: Ba‛asha assumes the reins of Yisra’ěl yet walks in the identical sins of his predecessor.
readings.text: [31] And the rest of the acts of Naḏaḇ, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [32] And there was fighting between Asa and Ba‛asha sovereign of Yisra’ěl all their days. [33] In the third year of Asa sovereign of Yehuḏah, Ba‛asha son of Aḥiyah became sovereign over all Yisra’ěl in Tirtsah, and reigned twenty-four years. [34] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and walked in the way of Yaroḇ‛am, and in his sin by which he had made Yisra’ěl sin.

readings.title: The Collision of the Divided Kingdom
readings.subtitle: Aḇiyah and Yaroḇ‛am draw up massive armies in the mountains of Ephrayim.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 13:1] In the eighteenth year of Sovereign Yaroḇ‛am, Aḇiyah began to reign over Yehuḏah. [2] He reigned three years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Miḵayahu the daughter of Uri’ěl of Giḇ‛ah. And there was fighting between Aḇiyah and Yaroḇ‛am. [3] And Aḇiyah joined battle with an army of mighty men of battle, four hundred thousand choice men. And Yaroḇ‛am drew up in battle formation against him with eight hundred thousand choice men, mighty brave men.

readings.title: The Indictment from the Mountain
readings.subtitle: Aḇiyah contrasts Yehuḏah's guardianship of the Charge with Yisra’ěl's golden calves.
readings.text: [4] And Aḇiyah stood on Mount Tsemarayim, which is in the mountains of Ephrayim, and said, “Hear me, Yaroḇ‛am and all Yisra’ěl: [5] “Do you not know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl has given the reign over Yisra’ěl to Daviḏ forever, to him and his sons, by a covenant of salt? [6] “Yet Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, the servant of Shelomoh son of Daviḏ, rose up and rebelled against his master. [7] “And vain men gathered to him, sons of Beliya‛al, and strengthened themselves against Reḥaḇ‛am son of Shelomoh, when Reḥaḇ‛am was young and tender of heart and could not be strong against them. [8] “And now you think to be strong against the reign of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which is in the hand of the sons of Daviḏ. And you are a large crowd, and with you are the gold calves which Yaroḇ‛am made for you as mighty ones. [9] “Have you not thrown out <dn>את</dn> the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the sons of Aharon, and the Lěvites, and made for yourselves priests, like the peoples of the lands, so that whoever comes to ordain himself with a young bull and seven rams then becomes a priest of what are not mighty ones? [10] “But as for us, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is our <dn>Elohim</dn>, and we have not forsaken <dn>Him</dn>, and priests are serving <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the sons of Aharon and the Lěvites, in the work, [11] and are burning to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> every morning and every evening ascending offerings and sweet incense, and the showbread is set on the clean table, and the lampstand of gold with its lamps to burn every evening, for we are guarding the Charge of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>. But you have forsaken <dn>Him</dn>. [12] “And see, with us as Head is <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>Himself</dn>, and <dn>His</dn> priests with sounding trumpets to sound the alarm against you. O children of Yisra’ěl, do not fight against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers, for you are not going to prosper!”

readings.title: Victory Through Absolute Reliance
readings.subtitle: Hemmed in by ambush, Yehuḏah cries out and YeHoVaH shatters the forces of Yaroḇ‛am.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 13:13] But Yaroḇ‛am sent round an ambush to go behind them, so they were in front of Yehuḏah, and the ambush was behind them. [14] And Yehuḏah turned and saw the battle was both in front and behind them. Then they cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the priests sounded the trumpets. [15] And the men of Yehuḏah gave a shout. And it came to be, as the men of Yehuḏah shouted, that <dn>Elohim</dn> smote Yaroḇ‛am and all Yisra’ěl before Aḇiyah and Yehuḏah. [16] And the children of Yisra’ěl fled before Yehuḏah, and <dn>Elohim</dn> gave them into their hand. [17] And Aḇiyah and his people struck them with a great slaughter, and five hundred thousand choice men of Yisra’ěl fell slain. [18] And the children of Yisra’ěl were humbled at that time, while the children of Yehuḏah prevailed, because they relied on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers. [19] And Aḇiyah pursued Yaroḇ‛am and captured cities from him: Běyth Ěl with its villages, and Yeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages. [20] And Yaroḇ‛am did not regain power again in the days of Aḇiyahu. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smote him, and he died. [21] But Aḇiyah became strong, and took fourteen wives, and brought forth twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters. [22] And the rest of the acts of Aḇiyah, and his ways, and his words are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.

readings.title: The Dividend of True Restoration
readings.subtitle: Asa cleanses the land of foreign altars, securing a decade of divine rest and prosperity.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 14:1] So Aḇiyah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Daviḏ. And Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land rested ten years. [2] And Asa did what was good and what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>, [3] and removed <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-places of the stranger, and the high places, and broke down <dn>את</dn> the pillars and cut down <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrim, [4] and commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, and to do the Torah and the command. [5] And he removed <dn>את</dn> the high places and <dn>את</dn> the sun-pillars from all the cities of Yehuḏah, and the reign rested under him. [6] And he built cities of defence in Yehuḏah, since the land had rest and he had no fighting in those years, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had given him rest. [7] And he said to Yehuḏah, “Let us build these cities and make walls around them, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us, because we have sought <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>. We have sought, and <dn>He</dn> has given us rest all around.” So they built and prospered. [8] And Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Yehuḏah bearing shields and spears, and from Binyamin two hundred and eighty thousand men bearing shields and drew bows. All of them were mighty brave men.

readings.title: Trust When Vastly Outnumbered
readings.subtitle: Asa leans the full weight of the nation on YeHoVaH, routing the million-man army of Zeraḥ.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 14:9] And Zeraḥ the Kushite came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he came to Marěshah. [10] And Asa went out against him, and they set battle in array in the Valley of Tsephathah at Marěshah. [11] And Asa called to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>, and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, there is no one but You to help between the mighty and the powerless. Help us, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, for we rest on You, and in Your Name we go against this crowd. O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, You are our <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not let man prevail against You!” [12] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smote the Kushites before Asa and Yehuḏah, and the Kushites fled. [13] And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them to Gerar. And the Kushites fell, until none was left alive for them, for they were broken before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>His</dn> army. And they took very much spoil, [14] and struck all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon them. And they plundered all the cities, for there was exceedingly much spoil in them. [15] And they also struck the camps of the herdsmen, and captured many sheep and camels, and returned to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Conditional Presence of the Creator
readings.subtitle: The Spirit of Elohim emboldens Asa to eradicate the lawlessness plaguing the land.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 15:1] And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon Azaryahu son of Oḏěḏ. [2] And he went out to face Asa, and said to him, “Hear me, Asa, and all Yehuḏah and Binyamin. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you while you are with <dn>Him</dn>. And if you seek <dn>Him</dn>, <dn>He</dn> is found by you, but if you forsake <dn>Him</dn>, <dn>He</dn> forsakes you. [3] “And for many days Yisra’ěl has been without the true <dn>Elohim</dn>, and without a Torah priest, and without Torah. [4] “But in their distress they turned to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and they sought <dn>Him</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> was found by them. [5] “And in those days there was no peace to the one who went out, nor to the one who came in, for great disturbances were on all the inhabitants of the lands, [6] and they were beaten down, nation by nation, and city by city, for <dn>Elohim</dn> troubled them with every distress. [7] “But you, be strong and do not let your hands be feeble, for there is a reward for your work!”

readings.title: A National Return to the Torah
readings.subtitle: Yehuḏah and the sojourners bind themselves by oath to seek YeHoVaH with total dedication.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 15:8] And when Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oḏěḏ the prophet, he strengthened himself, and removed <dn>את</dn> the abominations from all the land of Yehuḏah and Binyamin and from the cities which he had taken in the mountains of Ephrayim, and restored <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that was before the porch of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [9] and gathered all Yehuḏah and Binyamin, and those who sojourned with them from Ephrayim, and Menashsheh, and Shim‛on, for they came over to him in great numbers from Yisra’ěl when they saw that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> was with him. [10] And they gathered together at Yerushalayim in the third new moon, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa, [11] and slaughtered to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on that day seven hundred bulls and seven thousand sheep from the spoil which they had brought. [12] And they entered into a covenant to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers with all their heart and with all their being; [13] and whoever would not seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl would be put to death, from small to great, from man to woman. [14] And they swore to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with a loud voice, with shouting and with trumpets and with shopharot. [15] And all Yehuḏah rejoiced concerning the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought <dn>Him</dn> with all their being. And <dn>He</dn> was found by them, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave them rest all around.

readings.title: No Compromise in High Places
readings.subtitle: Asa strips the sovereigness mother of her authority and pulverizes her Asherah image.
readings.text: [16] And he also removed <dn>את</dn> Ma‛aḵah, the mother of Asa the sovereign, from being sovereigness mother, because she had made an abominable image of Ashěrah. And Asa cut down <dn>את</dn> her abominable image, and crushed it, and burned it by the wadi Qiḏron. [17] Yet the high places were not removed from Yisra’ěl. However, the heart of Asa was perfect all his days. [18] And he brought into the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>את</dn> the set-apart items of his father and his own set-apart items: silver and gold and utensils. [19] And there was no more fighting until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
